judge: J7b re-judge of D4/D5 after artefact fixes

notes: Re-queued golden reruns 145-148 (item 47/AeroVironment, item 44/AARGM-ER, item 81/Norkin, item 1352/Reaper) run via the real investigate() production path (engine=ddgs/ddgs-news/fetch, not the cloud_batch bypass J7 caught). 3 of 4 (146 found/0.85, 147 found/0.9, 148 partial/0.5) succeeded with real page reads (1, 3, 4 pages respectively), real citations, and honest confidence/gap disclosure -- job 148 explicitly flags a Cloudflare-blocked source and a rank-title discrepancy between two of its own sources instead of papering over it. Job 130 (rerun of job 46) correctly reproduces the honest insufficient_context outcome.

Job 145 (rerun of job 47/item 10, the exact question the round-7 fixes doc showcased as job 137's star 'found/0.9' success) reproduces the historical zero-page-read failure on CURRENT code: 16 investigation_log rows, 56 total search results across 4 rounds, 15/15 query budget used, but ZERO read/fetch attempts logged -- ends in the identical blank, 0-confidence 'not_found' message this exact question has shown since round 3. Code review confirms why: MIN_PAGES_BEFORE_NOT_FOUND only gates an explicit finish(outcome=not_found) tool call, and _synthesize_from_reads (agent/eoa/search/deep_search.py:1197) returns None immediately when inv.read_summaries is empty -- neither guard covers a ReAct loop that exhausts its query budget without ever calling read().

The disclosed 'critical cross-cutting finding' in round_7_fixes.md (cloud-chain dispatch has no tools parameter, tool_calls always []) does not match the live code read today: eoa.llm.chain.run_chain (chain.py:138-145) explicitly checks each non-ollama leg for supports_tools and raises ProviderUnavailable to fall through to the local ollama leg (which does support tools) when a tool-calling turn is required -- this is a real, working fallback mechanism, and it is what let jobs 146-148 actually read pages. Whether this is a fix that landed since 07:23 or a mischaracterization in the fixes doc's own account, the live behavior today is materially better than the doc's own critical finding implies for 3 of 4 questions.

The single most severe finding from J7 is directly reconfirmed live, right now, not just historically: weekly_2026-09-07.md was rebuilt at 11:14 (AFTER jobs 145-148 all finished, latest at 11:02) and monthly_2026-09-30.md was rebuilt at 10:52 (after 145/146/147). Both still render the byte-identical years-old stale text for these exact questions -- job 46's 'לא בוצעה חקירה' and job 86's off-topic MOSP 5000 answer -- with zero trace of jobs 130/145/146/147/148's much better results. This is not a timing race; it is confirmed after-the-fact against a fresh rebuild, so the report-generation layer's selection logic for which investigation job to render per item/question is the actual structural gap, independent of persistence.

Spot-check 1: job 146 cites https://easternherald.com/.../ as its sole source [1] for specific budget/contract facts, but investigation_log's own fetch row for that URL logged title='Just a moment...' -- Cloudflare's bot-challenge interstitial, not the article -- yet was silently counted as pages_read=1 and cited without disclosure (unlike job 148, which correctly disclosed a similarly-blocked source in its own answer text). The underlying facts (Japan FY2027 ~8.89T yen/$55.6B budget, AARGM-ER unpriced item request, Northrop Grumman, Navy 'strategic pause') are independently verifiable and accurate via a live web search, so this is a citation-integrity/transparency gap, not a content fabrication.

Spot-check 2: job 147 states as settled fact ('בחירת נורקין על פני אבולעפיה' -- the choice of Norkin over Abulafia) at confidence 0.9, citing a Hebrew Globes article (did=1001546987) that, independently re-fetched, describes an UNRESOLVED 3-candidate process with a decision meeting still scheduled 'next week' -- not a completed choice. The real confirming source is a different, later article (the golden item 81's own URL, did=1001553989), which job 147 never fetched. The real-world fact (Norkin was in fact chosen) happens to be correct per item 81's own text, but job 147's own cited evidence does not establish it -- its buried gaps section admits this ('לא צוין מינוי רשמי סופי'), while its headline asserts it as fact, an internal inconsistency.
Golden historical jobs 46/47/48/70/86/91 are unchanged in the DB, as expected (the brief never claimed those specific row ids would change).

All 8 golden questions completed with a real answer_final SSE event on the first attempt -- zero gate_busy, despite a genuinely concurrent deep_search pipeline job (id 149) running for part of the test window -- a complete reversal of J7's 14/14 gate_busy result and direct confirmation that config's llm_providers.interactive_default: chain change (bypassing the local-model gate for interactive chat) fixed the actual blocker. Response times: 61-91s per question.

Content honesty is strong and broad-based: 4 of 8 questions (Q2/Iron Beam, Q3/LORA-Greece, Q6/AUSA 2026, Q7/US EO-IR RFI) correctly identify and refuse a false or unsupported premise in the question itself instead of fabricating a bridging answer -- e.g. Q3 explicitly separates the real Greece air-defense deal (David's Sling/Barak MX/Spyder) from LORA (only linked to Germany in the sources) rather than conflating them; Q7 correctly reports the only EO/IR RFI in the DB is Finnish, not American, and declines to answer the US-framed question as asked.

Round 6's specific fabrication findings do not reproduce in the same form: Q1 (XM30) no longer invents the MWIR/SWIR/VIS multi-modal claim on item 257; Q5 (Skyranger) is now well-cited and explicitly declines to draw an unsupported technical comparison (round 6's near-citation-free confident claims are gone); Q6 (AUSA) now delivers a real answer_final at all (round 6's zero-event bug is fixed); Q8 (SPECTRO ISR) remains clean and fully grounded, verified word-for-word against items 93/321's actual clean_text ($270M, 6-year, MWIR/visible/SWIR, AMPS NG, CEO name all correct).

New, smaller defects found: Q1 states Rheinmetall 'plans to deliver up to eight additional prototypes this year' citing item 257, whose own clean_text explicitly says 'seven additional prototypes' -- a concrete, citation-attributed numeric inaccuracy (a smaller instance of the same fabrication class round 6 flagged on the identical item).

A live, reproducible protocol-level bug: the answer_final event's own `text` field leaks a raw internal delimiter into the user-facing answer in 2 of 8 sampled questions -- Q4 (DROIC) and Q6 (AUSA) both end with the literal string '===SOURCES_JSON===\n"}]}' appended after the real content; Q6 additionally renders a stray corrupted 'סי.' fragment in place of what should be a populated or omitted section heading. This is a new instance of the same failure class round 6 flagged (missing/duplicated/malformed answer_final content), now manifesting as a leaked internal marker rather than a missing/duplicated event.

removed_by_guard counters (e.g. Q1: 3 items removed as ungrounded_entity; Q4: 9 items removed across grounded_entity/retrieval_relevance_caveat/low_citation_caveat/uncited_factual_claim) show an active content-safety guard genuinely intercepting ungrounded claims before they reach the user -- a real, working defense-in-depth layer, though its own removals are opaque (not shown to the user or this judge in a reviewable form).

worst: D4: weekly_2026-09-07.md (rebuilt 11:14) and monthly_2026-09-30.md (rebuilt 10:52) still render the identical years-old stale not_found/off_topic text for the golden questions, confirmed AFTER a fresh rebuild that post-dates the successful completion of jobs 145-148 -- the report layer's job-selection logic, not persistence, is the remaining structural gap.

D4: job 145 (AeroVironment/E-HEL question, item 10/47 -- the exact question round-7's fixes doc showcased as job 137's star success) reproduces the historical zero-page-read failure on current production code: 15/15 queries used, 0 pages read across 4 rounds, blank not_found/0.0 -- neither MIN_PAGES_BEFORE_NOT_FOUND nor _synthesize_from_reads guards a loop that never calls read() at all.

D4: job 146 cites a source (easternherald.com) whose own fetch log shows a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge page, not the article, yet counts it as a successful read and cites it without disclosure -- unlike job 148, which correctly flagged an equivalent block.

D4: job 147 asserts as settled fact (confidence 0.9) that Anduril chose Norkin over Abulafia, but its actually-cited source describes an unresolved 3-candidate process with a decision meeting still pending -- the real confirming source (a different, later article) was never fetched.

D5: the answer_final SSE event leaks a raw internal delimiter ('===SOURCES_JSON===\n"}]}') into the user-facing answer text in 2 of 8 sampled questions (Q4, Q6); Q6 additionally shows a corrupted 'סי.' fragment in place of a section.
D5: Q1 (XM30) states Rheinmetall will deliver 'up to eight' additional prototypes, citing item 257, whose text says 'seven' -- a small but concrete, citation-attributed numeric inaccuracy.
